title: All About Hoverflies
checkpoint: Phase 5 complete (School readiness) — non-fiction, Phonics Screening Check review week, real facts about hoverflies.
note_for_grown_ups: Phase 5 complete (School readiness) — non-fiction, Phonics Screening Check review week, real facts about hoverflies.

pages.text: Nell spots a bug that looks just like a bee.
pages.illustration: Nell the bee hovering near a yellow-and-black striped bug that looks similar to her, by some flowers.

pages.text: This bug can not sting at all.
pages.illustration: A close-up of the striped bug, showing it has no sting at the back.

pages.text: This kind of bug is a hoverfly.
pages.illustration: A clear side view of the hoverfly resting on a leaf, wings folded.

pages.text: A hoverfly can hang still in the air.
pages.illustration: The hoverfly hovering perfectly still in mid-air above a flower bed.

pages.text: A hoverfly then zips off fast.
pages.illustration: The hoverfly darting away quickly in a sudden burst of speed.

pages.text: A hoverfly sips from bright flowers.
pages.illustration: The hoverfly resting on a bright flower, feeding from it.
The hoverfly moving between several bright flowers in a row, pollen visible on the petals.

pages.text: A hoverfly looks like a bee, but it is not.
pages.illustration: A side-by-side view of the hoverfly next to Nell the bee, showing how similar they look.

pages.text: Nell can tell it is not a bee.
pages.illustration: Nell the bee looking closely at the hoverfly, clearly telling the difference.

pages.text: Nell and the hoverfly both buzz off.
pages.illustration: Nell the bee and the hoverfly flying off together over the flower bed.
